svg.title: FinOps Gates Before Committing or Repatriating
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-finops-commitment-gates; chapter number: 5; title: FinOps Gates Before Committing or Repatriating; subtitle: Four checks that keep a discount from losing money; chart type: decision_tree; nodes: gate: G1; question: Is the commitment term no longer than the workload's predicted life?; pass next: G2; fail action: Shorten the term; a three-year plan on a two-year app wastes a full year.; gate: G2; question: Are existing RIs and savings plans overlaid before right-sizing?; pass next: G3; fail action: Overlay first, or the downsized VM leaves the reservation underutilized.; gate: G3; question: Does the FinOps agent start read-only or human-in-the-loop, with keys hidden by .gitignore?; pass next: G4; fail action: Lock the agent to read-only and confirm .gitignore before code leaves the box.; gate: G4; question: For repatriation, is the used server's BMC free of a vendor cloud license, with platform documentation?; pass next: Proceed and benchmark ESR against the 10.5% average and ~40.5% 98th percentile; fail action: Pass on the server.; caption: Policy becomes automation and automation becomes guardrails, but only after these gates hold.; assumptions note: Gate order is an editorial sequence; the ESR benchmark covers more than 1,400 data points with up to $2M per month in compute spend.; note: Sources: Intellipaat (7_L1_3-4kg8), FinOps Foundation (b7TiwS4_Ytw), AWS Events (JqwiGt78aOI), Craft Computing (JoqFD69bWLw), ProsperOps, a Flexera company (KW_LS_stgvc).

text.title: FinOps Gates Before Committing or Repatriating
text.tspan: FinOps Gates Before Committing or Repatriating

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Is the commitment term no longer than the workload's predicted life?; pass next: G2; fail action: Shorten the term; a three-year plan on a two-year app wastes a full year.
gate: G2; question: Are existing RIs and savings plans overlaid before right-sizing?; pass next: G3; fail action: Overlay first, or the downsized VM leaves the reservation underutilized.

gate: G3; question: Does the FinOps agent start read-only or human-in-the-loop, with keys hidden by .gitignore?; pass next: G4; fail action: Lock the agent to read-only and confirm .gitignore before code leaves the box.

gate: G4; question: For repatriation, is the used server's BMC free of a vendor cloud license, with platform documentation?; pass next: Proceed and benchmark ESR against the 10.5% average and ~40.5% 98th percentile; fail action: Pass on the server.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order is an editorial sequence; the ESR benchmark covers more than 1,400 data points with up to $2M per month in compute spend.
